ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The solid in the attached figure is composed of 14 unit white cubes. It can be seen that the bottom layer has 10 cubes connected into one piece; another 4 cubes are respectively stacked on bottom-layer cubes on the left side, back side, middle-front slightly to the right, and right side, forming 4 positions that are two layers high. Reasoning: The entire outer surface, including the bottom face, is painted red, so one face of a small cube is not painted red if and only if this face originally had face-to-face contact with another small cube. Therefore the number of red faces = 6 - the number of contacting neighbors; to have exactly 4 red faces, it must have exactly 2 contacting neighbors. First look at the 4 upper-layer cubes: each touches only the cube directly below it and has no side contact with cubes in the same layer, so each of them has 5 red faces and is not counted. Then scan the 10 bottom-layer cubes: among them, the 4 bottom-layer cubes with upper-layer cubes stacked on them, besides contact above, also contact adjacent cubes in the bottom layer, so their number of contacts is not 2; among the remaining connected bottom-layer cubes, counting the face-to-face adjacency relationships one by one according to the figure, exactly 6 cubes have 2 contacting neighbors. So there are 6 cubes with exactly 4 red faces in total.

method.method_draft: Use an adjacency-count scan of the individual cubes. From the image, first decompose the solid into the 14 unit cubes shown: a lower connected layer with several cubes, and four cubes stacked one level higher at the left, rear, middle/front-right, and right positions. From the text, all exterior faces, including the bottom, are painted before separation. The bridge rule is: a cube has exactly four red faces iff exactly two of its six faces were touching other cubes before painting. Now inspect each cube in the drawing and count its face-to-face neighbors. The four top cubes each touch only the cube below, so they have five red faces and are excluded. For the lower cubes, count horizontal neighbors plus a vertical neighbor if another cube sits on top. Mark exactly those lower cubes whose total number of touching neighbors is 2. This visual adjacency scan gives 6 such cubes.

method.method_draft: Use a layer/height-map method. From the image, redraw the solid as a top-view footprint of lower-layer positions, recording height 1 or height 2 at each position; the four height-2 positions correspond to the visible vertical stacks, and the total cube count should check against the text total of 14. From the text, both top/bottom and side exterior faces are painted. Apply separate formulas by height: for a height-1 cube, red faces = bottom + top + exposed horizontal sides, so it has exactly four red faces iff it has exactly two exposed side directions, equivalently two horizontal neighbors in the footprint. For the lower cube in a height-2 column, the top face is not painted, so red faces = bottom + exposed horizontal sides; it has exactly four red faces iff it has three exposed side directions, equivalently one horizontal neighbor in the footprint. The upper cube in each height-2 column is isolated at its level in the drawing and has five red faces, so it is not counted. Applying these tests to the height map of the pictured figure gives 6 qualifying cubes.

因此 exactly 4 个红面的 individual cubes 数量为 6。
